/blogs/third-party-car-insurance-claim-c.title: Keep your insurer’s file separate from the other driver’s
paragraphs: Write down each carrier, its claim number and the issue it is handling. An estimate sent to one carrier may never reach the other. If you receive a proposed release, record which carrier sent it and which claim it identifies. Ask about any differences in the information the two carriers want before providing the same packet to both.
/blogs/third-party-car-insurance-claim-c.linkLabel: Read more about keeping insurance requests organized

/blogs/what-happens-when-car-is-totaled-.title: Compare the valuation report with your actual vehicle
paragraphs: Check the trim, mileage, options and condition entries before looking at the final number. Record each mismatch alongside a photo, purchase record or other proof. If a comparison vehicle differs in a way that changes its usefulness, identify the specific feature or condition. A short list of documented discrepancies gives the adjuster something concrete to review. Keep the rental cutoff date with the valuation correspondence so you can plan transportation while a value dispute is being reviewed.
/blogs/what-happens-when-car-is-totaled-.linkLabel: Confirm rental approval and the return date

/blogs/what-is-auto-liability-insurance-.title: Identify whose policy you are reading
paragraphs: Write down the policyholder, covered vehicle and dates shown on the document. Mark whether the request concerns property damage or injuries. If a driver was borrowing the car or working, include that question in your notes before you search for the correct policy. The policy name alone may leave the most useful part of the coverage question unresolved.
/blogs/what-is-auto-liability-insurance-.linkLabel: Read how borrowed-car coverage can be evaluated

/blogs/car-insurance-deductible-after-ac.title: Reconcile the deductible with the shop invoice
paragraphs: Compare the final shop invoice with the insurer’s payment summary. Record who received the insurer’s payment, what you paid the shop and whether another payment is expected. Keep the deductible entry separate from any charge the shop says the carrier did not approve. If the carrier later sends a reimbursement, match it to the claim number.

/blogs/does-car-insurance-follow-the-car.title: Write down who gave permission and when
paragraphs: If someone borrowed a vehicle, save messages showing who offered it, the intended use and who drove. Gather both drivers’ and owners’ insurance information if available. Record which carrier has received a notice and which coverage question it is reviewing. Keep the facts about permission separate from anyone’s assumptions about which policy will pay.
/blogs/does-car-insurance-follow-the-car.linkLabel: Read how auto liability coverage works

/blogs/what-is-an-insurance-adjuster-car.title: Send a follow-up that identifies the unresolved question
paragraphs: After a call, note what the adjuster asked for, what you already supplied and the promised date for the next update. If you send a document, describe the one question it addresses. Keep the original file and a copy of the message. That makes it easier to see if the next request repeats an earlier one or asks for something different.
/blogs/what-is-an-insurance-adjuster-car.linkLabel: See more questions about insurance communications

links.label: Responding to a denied California car insurance claim

/blogs/cali-lean-vs-carolina-squat-whats.title: Document the vehicle setup before drawing conclusions
paragraphs: If vehicle height is relevant to a crash, keep photos showing the front, rear and side from a level position. Save any modification invoices or inspection records you have. If visibility is disputed, identify what the driver says was blocked and where the other vehicle or person was located. Keep measurements separate from conclusions about how the crash happened.
/blogs/cali-lean-vs-carolina-squat-whats.linkLabel: See how vehicle evidence fits into an investigation

/blogs/california-window-tint-laws.title: Record the window and test result a notice identifies
paragraphs: Save a copy of the notice and check which window it refers to. If you have an installation receipt or a measurement, keep it with the date and identifying details. After any corrective work, retain the new invoice and any follow-up paperwork. These records are easier to compare when each one identifies the same window and vehicle.
/blogs/california-window-tint-laws.linkLabel: Read about another citation issue and its effect on a claim

/blogs/digital-license-plates.title: Capture plate and vehicle details from the same record
paragraphs: Keep a clear photo of the plate, the vehicle and its location when those details matter to a collision. If the display was hard to read, preserve the original photo and share what you can see with the investigating agency or insurer. Keep registration confirmation and vendor correspondence separately so you can distinguish a display question from a question about the registration itself.
/blogs/digital-license-plates.linkLabel: Read how to track California crash reporting

/blogs/owi-vs-dui-in-the-us.title: Use the charge written on the paperwork
paragraphs: Before comparing OWI and DUI terminology, note the state, the exact charge and the agency or court named on the document. If the same event led to an injury claim, keep the claim records in a different file. A citation and an insurance review involve different questions, so record the dates, contacts and documents for each separately.
/blogs/owi-vs-dui-in-the-us.linkLabel: Read the California-specific impaired driving guide

/blogs/state-of-personal-injury-2026-ca-.title: Ask what a trend can tell you about an individual case
paragraphs: When a report describes rising claim costs or longer claim reviews, check its time period, location and what is being counted. Then identify which of those measures matches your actual question. For example, ask which records are still pending in your own file before using a statewide figure to estimate when you might hear back.
/blogs/state-of-personal-injury-2026-ca-.linkLabel: Read what influences an individual claim timeline

/blogs/what-happens-if-you-drive-without.title: Track the citation and the collision investigation separately
paragraphs: Keep the citation date, response instructions and status paperwork together. In a separate folder, save collision photos, witness details and insurer letters. If someone says the licensing question settles responsibility, ask which evidence shows the movement or decision that caused the crash. The two records can be useful even when they answer different questions.
/blogs/what-happens-if-you-drive-without.linkLabel: Read what can affect a fault determination

/blogs/california-bicycle-accident-guide.title: Record a blocked bike lane before the scene changes
paragraphs: If it is safe, take a wider picture showing where the bike lane was blocked, what space was available to go around and how approaching traffic could see you. Save any ride recording that shows why you changed course. Note if the obstruction moved or disappeared before an officer arrived so a later scene photo can be read in context.
/blogs/california-bicycle-accident-guide.linkLabel: See how a bicycle injury claim is investigated

/blogs/california-catastrophic-injury-gu.title: Keep a dated record of family support after discharge
paragraphs: On a calendar, note who helped with transportation, meals, appointments and other daily tasks. Save records of paid care separately from the time relatives volunteered. If a provider changes a recommendation, mark when the new plan began. The calendar can show how the arrangements changed without asking family members to reconstruct months of care later.
/blogs/california-catastrophic-injury-gu.linkLabel: Read what evidence can document long-term needs

/blogs/california-dog-bite-accidents-gui.title: Keep a record of the report before details are lost
paragraphs: Write down the date you reported the incident, the office that took the information and any reference it gave you. Preserve messages naming the animal or person who was supervising it. If someone gives you an updated name or address later, note where the information came from and keep the earlier account intact.
/blogs/california-dog-bite-accidents-gui.linkLabel: Read about evidence in dog bite cases

/blogs/california-motorcycle-accident-gu.title: Document repairs before they change the evidence
paragraphs: Ask the shop which parts it plans to remove or replace, and save any photographs it has taken. Keep your own wider images of the motorcycle and close-ups of affected areas. If an adjuster wants to inspect the bike, confirm where it is and how long it will stay there before work begins.

Keep the declarations for the motorcycle beside the repair estimate. Identify the policy period, covered bike and any equipment endorsement so an inspection or valuation question can be matched to the coverage being reviewed.
/blogs/california-motorcycle-accident-gu.linkLabel: Check the motorcycle policy and coverage for each loss

/blogs/california-pedestrian-accident-gu.title: Record the view from the driver’s approach
paragraphs: If it can be done safely, document what is visible from the approach to the crosswalk or driveway, including signs, parked vehicles or other obstructions. Mark where you were standing and where you were moving. Use those details to explain the scene to someone who has never been there.
/blogs/california-pedestrian-accident-gu.linkLabel: Read what a pedestrian investigation can involve

/blogs/california-personal-injury-guide.title: Make a one-page record before your consultation
paragraphs: Write down the incident date, your current treatment and the next decision you face. Add the agency or business that took a report and the insurers that have contacted you. Place any deadline at the top. A one-page overview can direct the conversation to the right issue while your larger record stays available for later review.
/blogs/california-personal-injury-guide.linkLabel: See what to bring to the first consultation

/blogs/california-rideshare-accidents-gu.title: Describe who was in the vehicle when the crash happened
paragraphs: Record whether the passenger was in the car, getting in or waiting to be picked up. Keep the name of the person who booked and copies of any pickup change messages. If the app updated the ride after the crash, save that notice alongside the original receipt. Times and account records can help reconstruct the sequence.
/blogs/california-rideshare-accidents-gu.linkLabel: Read the rideshare accident service guide

/blogs/california-slip-and-fall-accident.title: Trace your route to the exact spot
paragraphs: Write down the entrance you used, which direction you were walking and where your footing changed. If you can safely photograph the area, take both close and wide views. Save the receipt or other timestamp from your visit. A report that identifies a store but omits the doorway or aisle can be difficult to match to a maintenance or camera record.
/blogs/california-slip-and-fall-accident.linkLabel: Read a California court example about store inspections

/blogs/california-truck-accident-guide.title: Separate dispatch details from the crash timeline
paragraphs: Write down what you learned about the operator and the trailer, along with how each fact was identified. Use photos and the agency report to establish where the impact occurred. Keep dispatch, delivery and vehicle ownership questions in a separate list so they do not get confused with what a witness saw on the road.
/blogs/california-truck-accident-guide.linkLabel: Read about the records a truck operator may hold

/blogs/california-wrongful-death-guide.title: Create one contact list for the family
paragraphs: Keep a private list of which agency, insurer, employer or provider has contacted the family and what each asked for. Save the original letters, note their response dates and agree who will keep the list current. If someone is asked to sign for another person, set aside that document for individual review.
/blogs/california-wrongful-death-guide.linkLabel: Read what the office can discuss with a family

/blogs/disneyland-deaths.title: Separate the date of an incident from later reporting
paragraphs: When reviewing a reported fatal incident, record the incident date, the source’s publication date and the relationship between the incident and the later account. Note who supplied any finding about the location or cause. Those details help tell apart a contemporaneous report, an official finding and a later article repeating someone else’s description.
/blogs/disneyland-deaths.linkLabel: Read how incident records are evaluated in an injury claim

/blogs/fullerton-uber-lyft-accident-lawy.title: Pin down the pickup before sharing the incident location
paragraphs: Save messages that moved a pickup from one Fullerton entrance or curb to another. If the app shows a default pin, note where the vehicle actually stopped and what time the passenger got in. Keep the receipt, incident location and report number together so each can be matched to the correct trip.
/blogs/fullerton-uber-lyft-accident-lawy.linkLabel: See how the office approaches rideshare cases

/blogs/workers-comp-step-by-step-process.title: Keep a log of forms and work restrictions
paragraphs: Record the date you gave notice, the person who received it and the form or message you sent. File provider restrictions with any change in duties or hours your employer documented. If a letter requests a response, keep it with its stated date and the record of how you replied.
/blogs/workers-comp-step-by-step-process.linkLabel: Read how to organize treatment and work records

/blogs/blunt-force-trauma-determining-li.title: Match a description of impact to its source
paragraphs: Record what struck the person, what part of the event you observed and which facts came from someone else. Keep the equipment or scene description separate from the clinician’s findings. If the accounts describe different points of contact, label each source and date so a reviewer can compare them without confusing observation with inference.

If the injury was fatal, keep the accident evidence with any correspondence the family has received. A separate review can identify family relationships, available records and the scope of a proposed release.
/blogs/blunt-force-trauma-determining-li.linkLabel: Preparing a wrongful death claim review

/blogs/buena-park-wrongful-death-attorne.title: Keep a private list of records the family already has
paragraphs: Start with the agency reference, any letters and the names of the family members or representatives who received them. For an incident in Buena Park, keep the exact location and agency name together. A short inventory can help the office identify which document to ask for without collecting sensitive family material before it is needed.
/blogs/buena-park-wrongful-death-attorne.linkLabel: Find Buena Park office and local reporting information

/blogs/new-year-alcohol-related-crashes.title: Preserve the events around a late-night trip
paragraphs: Keep ride confirmations, messages about a pickup and any dashcam footage leading up to the crash. Pay attention to the date change at midnight when labeling screenshots or asking a business to look for video. An approximate time range and direction of travel can be more useful than saying only that it happened on New Year’s Eve.
/blogs/new-year-alcohol-related-crashes.linkLabel: Read the California impaired driving guide

/blogs/californias-minimum-speed-law.title: Describe the road conditions alongside the speed
paragraphs: If speed is disputed, write down the lane, traffic conditions, visibility and whether there was a hazard or a queue ahead. Save any usable time and location data from a recording. Keep estimated speeds labeled as estimates. That detail can help distinguish the number someone recalls from the circumstances they were responding to.
/blogs/californias-minimum-speed-law.linkLabel: Read how traction and road conditions can affect a crash

/blogs/car-accidents-what-is-a-skid-and-.title: Keep the seconds before the skid in the record
paragraphs: When saving video, include the approach and the driver’s movements before the wheels lost grip. Write down the road surface, weather and vehicle condition you actually observed. If you saw the car’s position only after the skid, describe that timing. The final position may answer a different question from the initial loss of traction.
/blogs/car-accidents-what-is-a-skid-and-.linkLabel: Read how vehicle and road evidence are evaluated

/blogs/the-safest-cars-to-drive-in-the-u.title: Compare safety ratings for the exact model year
paragraphs: Write down the year, trim and safety equipment for each vehicle you are considering. Check which test and testing year a rating represents. When two versions differ in equipment, record that difference with the score. This gives you a way to compare the vehicles available to you without assuming that a nameplate always comes with the same configuration.
/blogs/the-safest-cars-to-drive-in-the-u.linkLabel: Read what matters if a vehicle is involved in a crash

/blogs/diminished-value-claim-california.title: Compare vehicles at the same level of detail
paragraphs: Keep the repair history, date of the estimate, mileage and vehicle configuration together. For each comparison vehicle, record where the listing came from and which details differ from your car. A price by itself leaves too much unclear. A record of comparable features gives you a basis for explaining the value estimate to a reviewer.
/blogs/diminished-value-claim-california.linkLabel: Read how a total loss valuation is reviewed

/blogs/insurance-how-does-gap-insurance-.title: Check which balance the GAP provider is using
paragraphs: Put the lender’s dated payoff, the insurer’s settlement statement and the specific GAP contract side by side. If their numbers disagree, ask which date each document uses and whether it includes fees, add-ons or outstanding payments. Save the provider’s response with those records so you can see what was accepted and what is still disputed.
/blogs/insurance-how-does-gap-insurance-.linkLabel: Read what the auto insurer’s total loss figure represents

/blogs/notify-the-california-dmv-about-a.title: Keep proof of each report you submit
paragraphs: Use separate entries for the DMV, the investigating agency and each insurer. Record when you sent the form or notice, its reference number and any confirmation that came back. If you correct information later, keep a copy of the original and the correction so the reporting timeline remains clear.

/blogs/california-seat-belt-laws.title: Record the seat and restraint involved
paragraphs: When a restraint issue matters to a collision record, write down where each person was seated and what equipment or adjustment they were using. Save any photographs of the seat, belt or restraint label you already have. If some information came from a later inspection, record the source and date so it can be distinguished from observations at the scene.
/blogs/california-seat-belt-laws.linkLabel: Read how disputed facts affect injury claims

/blogs/is-california-a-no-fault-state-or.title: Separate who caused the crash from who is reviewing a bill
paragraphs: Mark which carrier accepted each claim and what kind of coverage it is reviewing. A communication about a vehicle estimate may leave the injury claim open. If the other driver’s insurer asks for something, keep its request with its own claim number and compare it with the notices you received from your policy.
/blogs/is-california-a-no-fault-state-or.linkLabel: Read what happens when you contact another driver’s insurer

/blogs/what-is-impaired-driving-in-calif.title: Keep first-hand observations separate from labels
paragraphs: If a witness described unusual driving, record the movement they saw, the location and the time. Save any recording instead of relying on a short description of it. Keep a collision report, a citation and an insurance request in separate files. Each may address different facts about the incident.
/blogs/what-is-impaired-driving-in-calif.linkLabel: Read how evidence helps establish fault

/blogs/traumatic-brain-injury-evidence-a.title: Use specific dated observations in the recovery timeline
paragraphs: Keep records of appointments and clinician instructions. If you or a relative are recording changes in routine, note details such as when someone started helping with scheduling or rides. Write down who observed the change and preserve the original description. Bring clinical questions to the treating provider so those questions can be addressed alongside the observations.
/blogs/traumatic-brain-injury-evidence-a.linkLabel: Read how daily effects can be documented

/blogs/california-uninsured-driver-hit-a.title: Record how you identified the other vehicle
paragraphs: Keep original pictures or video and note who supplied them. If a plate number is partial or came from someone else, label that uncertainty. Save the agency reference and the carrier’s written request with the evidence. This makes it easier to act on new information without overstating what the original record showed.
/blogs/california-uninsured-driver-hit-a.linkLabel: Read how to track coverage and evidence requests

/blogs/how-long-car-accident-settlement-.title: Find the next milestone in your own file
paragraphs: Ask which item is outstanding, who will get it and when you can reasonably follow up. The answer may concern treatment records, an insurer’s coverage decision or review of a proposed release. Record the answer in the claim log. An update about one item can help you plan even when a final resolution date remains uncertain.
/blogs/how-long-car-accident-settlement-.linkLabel: Read how the different stages of a claim fit together

/blogs/california-comparative-fault-pers.title: Separate each driver’s action by time and location
paragraphs: If fault is disputed, draw the approach of each vehicle and mark where contact occurred. Next to each disputed action, write down whether it came from a witness, video, vehicle inspection or your own memory. A timeline that identifies its sources makes it easier to see which part of the insurance decision needs a response.
/blogs/california-comparative-fault-pers.linkLabel: Read the California Supreme Court opinion that adopted comparative negligence

/blogs/how-much-is-my-personal-injury-ca.title: Track which estimates are supported by current records
paragraphs: Make one list of amounts already documented and another of figures still awaiting support. Note whether each medical or wage figure is paid, owed, estimated or disputed. When a new document arrives, record which assumption it changes. This helps you see whether a revised estimate reflects new evidence or a different way of counting the same item.
/blogs/how-much-is-my-personal-injury-ca.linkLabel: Open the injury case value calculator

links.label: Documenting a crash that worsened an earlier injury

/blogs/uber-lyft-accident-insurance-cali.title: Keep the entire trip history when the app changes status
paragraphs: Save the receipt, booking and cancellation notices, and any app message showing a status change. Write down the crash time separately and identify how you obtained it. If different people can access different records, ask each to save their own copy. This can help avoid treating the end of a trip as the time of the crash.
/blogs/uber-lyft-accident-insurance-cali.linkLabel: Read how the trip record can help with a rideshare claim

/blogs/truck-accident-evidence-eld-recor.title: Write the record request around the event and unit number
paragraphs: Record the date, time, place and vehicle identifiers first. Then identify which record could answer the question, such as a timestamped driver activity record or video of the approach. If a tractor and trailer were involved, keep their identifiers separate. That makes it easier to direct an information request to the right source.
/blogs/truck-accident-evidence-eld-recor.linkLabel: Read the truck collision evidence guide

/blogs/california-personal-injury-deadli.title: Put the actual response date beside the document
paragraphs: Write down the event date, the name of the party or agency involved and any dates stated in the paperwork. Keep mailing or receipt details when you have them. If a letter says you must act, copy the exact wording into your private log and raise it promptly with the appropriate office or counsel.
/blogs/california-personal-injury-deadli.linkLabel: Read how deadlines fit into the first case review

/blogs/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-i.title: Make the evidence folder usable when someone else is helping
paragraphs: Have the person helping you keep a short index with the report number, insurer contacts and dates documents came in. Identify the original location of each photo or video before making a copy. Put the next appointment or response date on the front page. That leaves a clear record even if more than one person calls for information.
/blogs/what-to-do-after-a-car-accident-i.linkLabel: Find Buena Park office and local reporting resources

/blogs/car-insurance-claim-without-polic.title: Keep the agency response next to the claim request
paragraphs: If the agency says no written report is available, record who told you and when. Save any confirmation, call number or incident record. If the adjuster asks for a report later, send the agency response with your claim number and ask which other evidence it will accept for the coverage being reviewed.

If you discovered damage to an unattended car, record when it was last undamaged and when you found it. Keep that time window with the agency response so the insurer can see what you know about the incident.
/blogs/car-insurance-claim-without-polic.linkLabel: Documenting damage discovered on a parked vehicle

/blogs/correct-inaccurate-car-accident-p.title: Track which version each person has
paragraphs: When you receive a new page or supplement, note its date and compare it with the original. Keep a short list of which insurer or representative received each version. Ask the person reviewing your claim whether the new record addresses the disputed detail or whether they still need another source.

If Garden Grove Police prepared the report, use the local guide to connect the disputed entry with the agency request and any later supplement. Confirm the investigating agency before following a city-specific process.
/blogs/correct-inaccurate-car-accident-p.linkLabel: Garden Grove report requests and disputed details

/blogs/medical-bills-while-car-accident-.title: Match payments to the services they cover
paragraphs: When a payment appears on a statement, check the service date, account number and name of the payer. An imaging office and the clinician who read the image may bill separately. If a payment or adjustment seems to be missing, ask the billing office for the account history before adding the balance to your ledger.
/blogs/medical-bills-while-car-accident-.linkLabel: Read how to check medical payments coverage

/blogs/medical-payments-coverage-medpay-.title: Separate treatment dates from submission dates
paragraphs: For each bill, record the treatment date, when the provider sent it and when the carrier acknowledged it. If an insurer says a document arrived late, compare its explanation with your submission receipt. Keep a copy of the policy provision it identifies and the document you supplied. That gives you a specific timeline to discuss instead of relying on memory.
/blogs/medical-payments-coverage-medpay-.linkLabel: Review the wider medical billing file

/blogs/what-is-subrogation-car-insurance.title: Keep the demand and the distribution together
paragraphs: Save the original recovery demand with the final letter explaining what was collected. Compare the deductible entered in the demand with your receipt. If the final amount is smaller, ask which part reflects a partial recovery and which part reflects any allocated expenses. Keep the explanation with the payment so you can identify what remains unresolved.

If the next renewal also changes, request the rating explanation separately from the recovery letter. Match the accident date and driver so you can tell whether both departments are using the same record.
/blogs/what-is-subrogation-car-insurance.linkLabel: Review a separate change to your renewal premium

/blogs/rental-car-reimbursement-after-ac.title: Keep the return record with the authorization
paragraphs: Save the approval showing the last covered date and the branch receipt showing when you returned the car. If the insurer changes its position after a total loss decision, ask for a written explanation of the cutoff. Compare any later bill with those records before treating the amount as either covered or entirely your responsibility.
/blogs/rental-car-reimbursement-after-ac.linkLabel: Review the separate total loss decision

/blogs/what-to-do-if-someone-hits-your-p.title: Track the time window alongside each camera request
paragraphs: Record the earliest and latest supported time for the parked-car damage and the reason for each boundary, such as a receipt or earlier image. Keep that window beside each camera request. If a business supplies only part of the period, note the missing interval before concluding that no relevant vehicle appeared.
/blogs/what-to-do-if-someone-hits-your-p.linkLabel: Review claim evidence when a report is unavailable

/blogs/how-accidents-affect-car-insuranc.title: Keep a correction request with the renewal it concerns
paragraphs: Use the same accident date, vehicle and driver identifiers on your written request and supporting documents. Save the renewal notice before sending it. If the carrier later revises one figure, compare the revised declarations with that original notice so you can identify which change was made and whether another issue still needs a response.
/blogs/how-accidents-affect-car-insuranc.linkLabel: Prepare a focused request for the insurer

/blogs/california-motorcycle-insurance.title: Match the inspection request to the motorcycle claim
paragraphs: Record where the bike is stored, who has access and which carrier requested an inspection. Keep the VIN and claim number on the correspondence. If a shop or salvage company proposes moving it, ask how the pending inspection will be handled and retain the response with the pickup or repair authorization.
/blogs/california-motorcycle-insurance.linkLabel: Discuss motorcycle evidence and injury questions

links.label: Checking whether a device is a moped or motorized scooter

/blogs/mopeds-vs-scooters-california.title: Save the classification with the ride record
paragraphs: Keep the manufacturer label and model information with the receipt or rental trip identifier. If the device has been modified, identify which description applies to its condition on the incident date. Keep the route evidence separate from the medical timeline so a question about classification does not obscure what happened at the collision.

/blogs/car-insurance-claim-denied-califo.title: Record what changed after reconsideration
paragraphs: Keep the original denial beside the response to your new evidence. Identify whether the insurer changed its position on coverage, responsibility or one expense. If only part of the issue was resolved, write down what remains disputed before treating the review as complete.
/blogs/car-insurance-claim-denied-califo.linkLabel: Prepare a focused follow-up to the adjuster

/blogs/car-accident-pre-existing-injury-.title: Compare the same task before and after the crash
paragraphs: If your concern is a change in work or daily activity, choose a specific task and record the earlier level of functioning, the observed change and the supporting record. Keep a medical restriction separate from your own account of how the task felt. Both can matter without establishing the same fact.
/blogs/car-accident-pre-existing-injury-.linkLabel: Review how documented losses support a claim valuation
